__
 
• **Kabir** was a prominent poet-saint of the **Bhakti movement**, known for his devotional and philosophical poetry.

• Kabir was born in the 15th century in **Varanasi** (modern-day Uttar Pradesh, India), though his exact birth year is uncertain.
 
• He strongly opposed the rigid practices of both **Hinduism** and **Islam** and emphasized a universal path to spirituality.
 
• Kabir’s teachings revolved around the concepts of **love, unity, equality, and devotion to the Supreme Being**.
 
• His works are included in the **Guru Granth Sahib**, the holy scripture of Sikhism.
 
• Some of his famous dohas include teachings about **self-realization, truth, and the futility of rituals**.
 
• Kabir’s philosophy is often seen as a blend of **Hindu Bhakti** and **Sufi mysticism**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a longitudinal wave?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sound wave in air**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **longitudinal wave** is a type of wave in which the particles of the medium move parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
 
• **Sound waves in air** are a classic example of longitudinal waves because the air particles oscillate back and forth along the same direction in which the sound wave is traveling.
 
• The regions of compression (high pressure) and rarefaction (low pressure) are formed due to the oscillation of air particles.
 
• Sound waves require a **medium** for propagation; they cannot travel in a vacuum.
 
• Examples of longitudinal waves include sound waves in solids, liquids, and gases, as well as seismic P-waves.
 
• Longitudinal waves are characterized by properties such as **wavelength, frequency, amplitude, and speed.**
 
• They play a crucial role in various applications, including **communication technologies, sonar systems, and medical ultrasound.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Water wave on surface**__

 __
 
• **Water waves** are an example of **surface waves**, which are a combination of longitudinal and transverse motion.
 
• In water waves, particles move in circular or elliptical paths, creating both forward and backward motion.
 
• These waves are commonly observed on the surface of oceans, lakes, and other water bodies.
 
 
 
• **Light wave in vacuum**__
 __
 
• **Light waves** are **electromagnetic waves** and are transverse in nature.
 
• They do not require a medium for propagation and can travel through a vacuum.
 
• Light waves have both an electric field and a magnetic field oscillating perpendicular to each other and the direction of wave propagation.
 
 
 
• **Radio wave during transmission**__
 
 
• **Radio waves** are also a type of **electromagnetic wave** and are transverse in nature.
 
• They are used in various applications, such as **communication systems, broadcasting, and radar.**
 
• Like light waves, they can propagate through a vacuum.

questions.question: Which method used in metallurgy specifically describes the formation of metal oxides by heating carbonate ores?

__
 
• **Calcination** is a thermal process used in metallurgy to convert carbonate ores into metal oxides.
 
• It involves **heating the ore in the absence of air**, or a limited supply of air, which prevents the ore from melting.
 
• The process removes **volatile substances, water, and organic matter** from the ore and decomposes carbonate ores into oxides.
 
• An example of calcination is the conversion of **calcium carbonate (CaCO₃)** to calcium oxide (CaO) and carbon dioxide (CO₂).
 
• Calcination is commonly used for ores like **limestone, dolomite, and magnesite**.
 
• This process is crucial for purifying ores and preparing them for further reduction or extraction methods in metallurgy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This process is unrelated to metallurgy and does not involve heating ores or converting them to oxides.
 
 
 
• **Chlorination**__
 __
 
• **Chlorination** is a metallurgical process used for extracting metals like gold by reacting them with chlorine gas.
 
• This method is employed in cases where metals form stable chlorides, but it is not related to the conversion of carbonate ores into oxides.
 
 
 
• **Carbonation**__
 
 
• **Carbonation** refers to the process of dissolving carbon dioxide in liquids, commonly used in the production of carbonated beverages.
 
• This term does not apply to metallurgical processes and is unrelated to the heating of ores.

questions.question: A computer system mainly includes which three components?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Input, Processing, Output**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **computer system** is primarily based on three fundamental components: **Input, Processing, and Output**.
 
• **Input:** This component helps in feeding data or instructions into the computer system through input devices such as a **keyboard, mouse, scanner, or microphone.**
 
• **Processing:** The central processing unit (**CPU**) acts as the brain of the computer, performing calculations and logical operations to process the input data.
 
• **Output:** After processing, the computer system provides results or information through output devices such as **monitors, printers, or speakers.**
 
• This cycle of Input, Processing, and Output forms the core of all computer operations and is fundamental to its functioning.
 
• These components enable the computer to perform various tasks such as **data computation, storage, and retrieval.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **CPU, Scanner, Air Conditioner**__

 __
 
• The **CPU** (Central Processing Unit) is a key part of the computer system responsible for data processing.
 
• A **scanner** is an input device used to digitize physical documents or images but is not a primary component of a computer system.
 
• An **air conditioner** is not related to the computer system. It is used for cooling and maintaining temperature but has no direct role in the functioning of a computer.
 
 
 
• **Monitor, USB, Light**__
 __
 
• A **monitor** is an output device that displays processed information visually.
 
• A **USB** is a storage device or connector used to transfer data but is not a fundamental computer system component.
 
• **Light** is not a part of the computer system; it may refer to indicators or lighting used externally.
 
 
 
• **Mouse, CPU, Mobile**__
 
 
• A **mouse** is an input device used for pointing and selecting but is not one of the primary system components.
 
• The **CPU** is a vital processing component of the computer system.
 
• A **mobile device** is not part of the computer system's basic components; it is a separate technology used for communication and computing.

questions.question: What type of rainfall occurs when air is forced to rise over a mountain barrier?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Orographic rainfall**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Orographic rainfall** occurs when **moist air** is forced to ascend due to the presence of a **mountain barrier**.
 
• As the air rises, it cools and condenses, forming clouds and resulting in **precipitation** on the windward side of the mountain.
 
• The leeward side of the mountain, also known as the **rain shadow region**, receives significantly less rainfall.
 
• This type of rainfall is common in areas with prominent mountain ranges, such as the **Western Ghats in India**, the **Rocky Mountains** in North America, and the **Andes** in South America.
 
• Orographic rainfall plays a crucial role in shaping the **climate and vegetation** of mountainous regions.
 
• It is one of the three main types of rainfall, alongside **cyclonic** and **convectional rainfall**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cyclonic rainfall**__

 __
 
• **Cyclonic rainfall** occurs due to the interaction of **cold air masses** and **warm air masses**, leading to the formation of **cyclones**.
 
• This type of rainfall is associated with **low-pressure systems** and is common in regions experiencing **temperate cyclones** or **tropical cyclones**.
 
 
 
• **Convectional rainfall**__
 __
 
• **Convectional rainfall** occurs when the sun heats the earth's surface, causing the air to rise, cool, and condense.
 
• This type of rainfall is common in **equatorial regions** and during the summer months.
 
• It is typically associated with **short, intense showers** or **thunderstorms**.
 
 
 
• **Frontal rainfall**__
 
 
• **Frontal rainfall** occurs when a **warm air mass** meets a **cold air mass**, leading to condensation and precipitation along the **front**.
 
• This type of rainfall is common in **mid-latitude regions** and is associated with the movement of weather fronts.

questions.question: What makes basic rules in the Constitution effective?

options.text: They are based on popular customs only.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**They are legally enforceable**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Basic rules** in a Constitution are primarily designed to ensure the proper functioning of a state or country.
 
• These rules become **effective** because they are **legally enforceable**, meaning they can be upheld and implemented through courts or governing bodies.
 
• Legal enforceability ensures that these rules are binding on all citizens, institutions, and governments, creating a framework for governance.
 
• It establishes a system of **checks and balances**, ensuring that no one is above the law.
 
• For example, in India, the **Constitution** provides legal enforcement of fundamental rights through the **judiciary**, including the **Supreme Court** and **High Courts**.
 
• Legal enforceability safeguards **justice, equality, and liberty**, making the Constitution robust and effective.
 
• Without legal enforcement, the rules of the Constitution would merely be advisory and would lack the power to hold individuals or entities accountable.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **They are based on popular customs only**__

 __
 
• Popular customs are practices or traditions widely followed by people in a society. However, they are not legally binding unless codified into law.
 
• Constitutional rules go beyond customs as they are formally written and enforceable by the judiciary and government institutions.
 
• Examples of customs include traditional ceremonies or cultural practices, which may influence laws but lack direct legal enforceability.
 
 
 
• **They are a secret**__
 __
 
• Constitutional rules are not kept secret; they are publicly accessible documents meant to guide governance and ensure transparency.
 
• In democratic systems, the Constitution is available to all citizens, promoting awareness and understanding of their rights and duties.
 
 
 
• **They are not enforced**__
 
 
• If constitutional rules are not enforced, they lose their purpose and effectiveness.
 
• Enforcement is necessary to uphold legal order and protect the rights and freedoms of citizens.

The correct answer is __**Peaceful petitions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the early years, the **Indian National Congress (INC)** adopted a policy of **moderation** to achieve its objectives, primarily focusing on peaceful and constitutional methods.
 
• Congress leaders believed in persuading the British government through **petitions, speeches, and resolutions** to grant Indians limited self-governance.
 
• Leaders like **Dadabhai Naoroji, Surendranath Banerjee, and Gopal Krishna Gokhale** were prominent moderates who emphasized the use of **dialogue, diplomacy, and reforms**.
 
• The approach was based on the belief that the British government would respond to reason and justice if Indians showed their loyalty and expressed their demands peacefully.
 
• Key demands during this phase included **civil service reforms, more representation for Indians in the legislative councils, and economic relief measures**.
 
• This approach was reflective of the **early phase (1885–1905)** of the Indian freedom struggle, also known as the **Moderate Phase**.
 
• The **Indian Councils Act of 1892** was one of the outcomes of these peaceful petitions, which provided for limited legislative reforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Violent protests**__

 __
 
• The approach of violent protests was not adopted by Congress leaders during the early years. Violent methods were associated with **revolutionary groups** like the **Anushilan Samiti** and **Ghadar Party**, which emerged later as a reaction to British repression and the inefficacy of peaceful methods.
 
 
 
• **Foreign intervention**__
 __
 
• The idea of seeking foreign intervention to gain self-governance was not a strategy pursued by the Congress leadership. However, during the later phases, leaders like **Subhas Chandra Bose** sought foreign support (e.g., from Axis powers) for India’s independence.
 
 
 
• **Revolutionary wars**__
 
 
• Revolutionary wars or armed uprisings were not part of the Congress strategy in its early years. Such actions were characteristic of movements like the **1857 Revolt** or later revolutionary activities led by groups like the **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)**.

questions.question: Which of the following states recorded the second-highest population density in 2011 as per the Census of India?

• The population density of West Bengal was recorded as **1029 persons per square kilometer**, making it one of the most densely populated regions in the country.
 
• Population density is defined as the number of people living per unit of area, typically per square kilometer, and is an important demographic indicator.
 
• The high population density in West Bengal can be attributed to factors such as **urbanization, industrialization, fertile land, and the presence of major cities like Kolkata.**
 
• The state is located in the eastern part of India and is known for its **rich cultural heritage, major industries, and agricultural productivity.**
 
• West Bengal has a significant contribution to the Indian economy through industries like **jute, tea, chemicals, and leather.**
 
• The **Hooghly River basin** and coastal regions have supported a dense population due to favorable living conditions and economic opportunities.

• **Madhya Pradesh**__

 __
 
• **Madhya Pradesh**, located in central India, is known as the **"Heart of India"** due to its geographical location.
 
• The state has a relatively **low population density** compared to West Bengal, primarily due to its large area and significant forest cover.
 
• It is rich in natural resources, biodiversity, and cultural heritage, making it famous for sites like **Khajuraho, Sanchi, and Bandhavgarh National Park.**
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra**__

• **Maharashtra** is India's second-most populous state but does not rank as highly in population density due to its large geographical size.
 
• It is an economic powerhouse with industries like **finance, technology, entertainment, and manufacturing.**
 
• The state is home to Mumbai, India's financial capital, and Pune, a major IT and education hub.
 
 
 
• **Uttar Pradesh**__
 
 
• **Uttar Pradesh** has the **highest population** in India as per the Census 2011.
 
• It is India's most populous state and is known for its **historical significance, pilgrimage sites, and diverse culture.**
 
• Major cities include **Lucknow, Kanpur, Varanasi, and Agra.**

questions.question: Which of the following options best describes the purpose of the Red Data Book?

options.text: A list of protected forest areas
A compilation of forest conservation laws
A record of endangered plant and animal species

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**A record of endangered plant and animal species**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Red Data Book** is an internationally recognized document that provides a **comprehensive record of species that are endangered**, whether they are plants, animals, or fungi.
 
• The book is maintained by the **International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN)** and serves as a critical resource for conservationists and policymakers.
 
• This document highlights the **threatened and near-threatened species**, their current status, and the potential risks they face.
 
• It categorizes species into different risk levels, such as **critically endangered, endangered, and vulnerable**, based on their population trends and habitat conditions.
 
• It plays a key role in **raising awareness** about the need for species conservation and in guiding efforts to prevent extinction.
 
• The Red Data Book also acts as a reference for global efforts like the **Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD)** to ensure the protection of biodiversity.
 
• It helps identify regions or ecosystems that need **urgent attention and conservation measures**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **A list of protected forest areas**__

 __
 
• This option refers to specific areas designated for conservation, such as **national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, or biosphere reserves**, but it is not the purpose of the Red Data Book.
 
• Protected forest areas are instead documented in lists maintained by national governments and organizations like the **UNESCO World Heritage Centre**.
 
 
 
• **A compilation of forest conservation laws**__
 __
 
• Forest conservation laws include legal frameworks like the **Forest Conservation Act, 1980 (India)** or international agreements like the **Kyoto Protocol**.
 
• These laws aim to regulate the use of forests and prevent deforestation, but they are not a part of the Red Data Book.
 
 
 
• **A collection of tree species**__
 
 
• A collection of tree species may exist in botanical databases or floras, but the Red Data Book specifically focuses on **endangered species**, not on general cataloging of trees.

questions.question: How are the one-third reserved seats for women distributed across different categories in local bodies?

options.text: Only one-third of the general (unreserved) seats are reserved for women, excluding reserved-category seats.
One-third of all seats, including those reserved for SC/ST/OBC categories, are reserved for women, allowing a seat to be reserved simultaneously for a woman and for an SC/ST/OBC candidate.
One-third reservation applies only to leadership positions such as Sarpanch or Chairperson.
One-third reservation applies only to rural Panchayats and not to urban municipal bodies.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**One-third of all seats, including those reserved for SC/ST/OBC categories, are reserved for women, allowing a seat to be reserved simultaneously for a woman and for an SC/ST/OBC candidate.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **One-third reservation for women** in local bodies ensures political representation and empowerment for women.
 
• Under this provision, **one-third of all seats**, including those reserved for **Scheduled Castes (SC), Scheduled Tribes (ST), and Other Backward Classes (OBC)**, are allotted to women.
 
• This simultaneous reservation allows a seat to be reserved for both a **woman** and an **SC/ST/OBC candidate**, fostering inclusivity and diversity.
 
• This policy is implemented as per the provisions of the **73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments**, which introduced reservations for women in rural and urban local governance systems.
 
• The measure aims to encourage greater **women’s participation** in governance and decision-making processes at grassroots levels.
 
• The reservation applies to **both general seats and reserved-category seats**, ensuring equitable representation across all categories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: Only one-third of the general (unreserved) seats are reserved for women, excluding reserved-category seats**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because it limits the reservation to general seats only, excluding **SC/ST/OBC seats**, which contradicts the actual policy of inclusive reservation.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: One-third reservation applies only to leadership positions such as Sarpanch or Chairperson**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect as the reservation policy applies to **all seats** in local bodies, not just leadership positions.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: One-third reservation applies only to rural Panchayats and not to urban municipal bodies**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect because the reservation applies to both **rural Panchayats** and **urban municipal bodies**, as per the **73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments**.

questions.question: According to the Citizenship Act, how many years must a person ordinarily reside in India to apply for citizenship by naturalisation under general conditions?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Under the **Citizenship Act, 1955**, citizenship by naturalisation can be granted to a foreign national who has been ordinarily residing in India for at least **12 years** immediately preceding the application.
 
• This includes a requirement of **11 years of continuous residence** and 1 year of residence immediately before applying.
 
• The Act defines several modes of acquiring Indian citizenship, including **birth, descent, registration, and naturalisation**.
 
• Naturalisation requires the applicant to demonstrate **good character**, adequate knowledge of a language specified in the Constitution, and intention to reside in India.
 
• The aim of this provision is to ensure that applicants have a **strong connection** with India before being granted citizenship.
 
• The eligibility criteria for naturalisation are outlined under **Section 6** of the Citizenship Act, 1955.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **5 years**__

 __
 
• The period of **5 years** is incorrect because it applies to certain specific cases under the Citizenship Act, such as cases involving **registration** of citizenship under special provisions.
 
• It is not the general condition for naturalisation.

• The **7-year criterion** applies in cases of acquiring citizenship through **registration** under specific provisions of the Act, but not through naturalisation.
 
 
 
• **10 years**__
